AbstractText.Label: CONTEXT
AbstractText.content: Foam rolling is a popular intervention used by allied health professionals and the general population. Current research suggests that foam rolling may have an effect on the ipsilateral antagonist muscle group and produce a cross-over effect in the muscles of the contralateral limb. The purpose of this study was to examine the acute effects of foam rolling to the left quadriceps on ipsilateral antagonist hamstrings and contralateral quadriceps muscle group pressure pain threshold (PPT). Through this research, we sought to gather data to further develop the methodology for future studies of this intervention.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: Video-guided foam roll intervention on the left quadriceps musculature.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Ipsilateral hamstring (antagonist) and contralateral quadriceps muscle PPT.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: A significant difference was found between pretest to posttest measures for the ipsilateral hamstrings (t (20) = -6.2, p < 0.001) and contralateral quadriceps (t (20) = -9.1, p < 0.001) suggesting an increase in PPT.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: These finding suggest that foam rolling of the quadriceps musculature may have an acute effect on the PPT of the ipsilateral hamstrings and contralateral quadriceps muscles. Clinicians should consider these results to be exploratory and future investigations examining this intervention on PPT is warranted.
